milestones.name: Touchdown
milestones.summary: The rover has landed on the de Gerlache crater rim and deployed from the lander.
milestones.fact: The Soviet Luna 9 probe made the first soft landing on the Moon on February 3, 1966.
milestones.source: ESA, 3 February: Luna 9 (esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/3_February); NASA Science APOD text (science.nasa.gov/?p=1253718)

milestones.name: Odometer
milestones.fact: Apollo 17's Lunar Roving Vehicle covered about 36 km across three drives in December 1972.
milestones.source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Roving Vehicle (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/apollo_lrv.html): 35.9 km

milestones.name: Mapper
milestones.summary: The rover has surveyed {share}% of the map.
milestones.fact: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, launched in June 2009, maps the Moon; its laser altimeter, LOLA, measures the elevations used for polar terrain maps.

milestones.name: Crater descent
milestones.summary: The rover descended de Gerlache's inner wall, more than 150 m below the landing point, and climbed back out.
milestones.fact: With no wind or rain, lunar craters wear down only through small impacts, so they degrade over billions of years.
milestones.source: Fassett & Thomson (2014), Crater degradation on the lunar maria, JGR Planets, doi:10.1002/2014JE004698

milestones.name: Boulder field
milestones.summary: The rover crossed a boulder field on the rim of a fresh crater.
milestones.fact: Lunar boulders mostly come from impact ejecta, and the largest around young craters reach tens of meters across.
milestones.source: Pajola et al. (2019), boulder size-frequency distribution at Linné crater from LROC images (arxiv.org/abs/1812.00590)

milestones.name: Into the dark
milestones.summary: The rover entered the permanently shadowed crater and returned to sunlight.
milestones.fact: NASA's LRO Diviner instrument has measured temperatures near 25 K (about -248 °C) in permanently shadowed polar craters.
milestones.source: NASA SVS 11230, Diviner temperatures of the lunar poles (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11230): shadowed regions as cold as -414 °F; Paige et al. (2010), Science 330:479, doi:10.1126/science.1187726

milestones.name: Flare survivor
milestones.summary: A solar flare struck while the rover was protected. No damage was recorded.
milestones.fact: With almost no atmosphere or global magnetic field, the lunar surface is fully exposed to solar energetic particle events.
milestones.source: NASA Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, Working on the Moon: Radiation (nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/WOTM/WOTM-Radiation.html)

milestones.name: Clean run
milestones.summary: The rover completed all fourteen days without damage. The moonquake does not count: nothing can prevent it.
milestones.fact: ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 lander and Pragyan rover had a planned mission life of one lunar day, about 14 Earth days.

milestones.name: Crater layers
milestones.summary: The camera imaged the layered rock exposed in de Gerlache's inner wall.
milestones.fact: Impacts excavate material from below the surface, and crater walls can expose layers of older rock.
milestones.source: General impact-crater geology; not checked against a single source (fact-check note)

milestones.name: Regolith sample
milestones.summary: The drill collected a sample of lunar regolith, away from the ground the lander disturbed.
milestones.fact: The six Apollo landings brought back about 382 kg of lunar rock, core samples, pebbles, sand and dust.

milestones.name: Water ice
milestones.summary: The drill found water ice in the regolith inside the permanently shadowed crater.
milestones.fact: NASA's LCROSS probe struck Cabeus crater on October 9, 2009; the impact plume indicated about 5.6% water by mass in the regolith.
milestones.source: Colaprete et al. (2010), Detection of water in the LCROSS ejecta plume, Science 330:463, doi:10.1126/science.1186986 (5.6 ± 2.9%)

milestones.name: Earth on the horizon
milestones.summary: The camera photographed a sunlit Earth above the lunar horizon.
milestones.fact: From the lunar south pole Earth sits near the horizon, drifting a few degrees above and below it as the Moon librates.
milestones.source: Gorkavyi et al. (2023), Atmos. Meas. Tech. 16:1527, doi:10.5194/amt-16-1527-2023; NASA SVS 4944

milestones.name: Rim panorama
milestones.summary: The camera photographed the view from the de Gerlache crater rim.
milestones.fact: De Gerlache Rim 2 is one of nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole that NASA named for Artemis III in October 2024.
